title: Help
subtitle: How to get text from video and audio — common cases and every control.

brief.title: Brief — Design Document from Meeting
brief.intro: Brief generates a structured PDF design document from a recorded meeting. It uses an LLM to extract decisions, action items, open questions, and engineering design details.
brief.req_key: A Gemini API key (Settings → Transcription → Gemini API key).
brief.req_vtt: WebVTT enabled (the Brief chip auto-enables it).
brief.req_video: For screenshots: the source must have a video track. Audio-only files generate a text-only document.
brief.privacy: Your transcript and screenshots are sent to Google Gemini. Do not use Brief with confidential recordings unless you are on a Gemini data-protection plan.
brief.output: Saved as {stem}.brief.pdf next to the .txt transcript in the output folder.
brief.cost: Approximately $0.07 per 1-hour meeting using Gemini Flash. Free tier (60 req/min) is usually sufficient for one meeting at a time.

overview.title: What Video to Text does
overview.intro: Add local files, folders, or links (YouTube, TikTok, playlists, Castbox, and other sites yt-dlp supports). The app downloads or reads the media, extracts audio with ffmpeg, and writes a transcript.
overview.flow_1: Set the output folder and a profile (Simple / Quality / Power).
overview.flow_2: Add links or drop files into the queue.
overview.flow_3: Start the batch. Results land in the output folder as .txt (and optional siblings).
overview.profile_simple: Simple — links to plain text; captions used when available; advanced speakers / REST / Vision hidden.
overview.profile_quality: Quality — meeting-grade WebVTT and a strong Whisper model.
overview.profile_power: Power — Quality plus keep media, folder scan, SRT, cookies/Deno, and the full advanced panel.
overview.note: API keys, the output folder, and tool paths are never overwritten when you switch profiles. Save Preferences before you run — unsaved toggles do not apply to the next job.

cases.title: Common cases
cases.intro: Match your goal to the shortest path.
cases.c1_want: A TikTok or YouTube link as plain text
cases.c1_do: Profile Simple. Paste the link → Start batch. If the video has manual captions in a priority language, Whisper is skipped.
cases.c2_do: Profile Quality. General → Also save… → Export timed transcript as WebVTT. Mode On this computer, model large-v3. You get .txt and .vtt.
cases.c3_do: Same as timed subtitles, then Default video language = English (not Auto). Tools & advanced → Speaker labels → Label speakers. The queue row for that file must also say English. Re-run; the old file is not rewritten. Cues look like <v Person 1>…</v>.
cases.c4_want: Russian / Ukrainian / any language — who spoke
cases.c4_do: WebVTT on. Tools & advanced → Speakers (pyannote diarize): Hugging Face token + Python with pyannote, then enable Diarize speakers. Whisper language stays as you set it.
cases.c5_want: A whole playlist or a Castbox show
cases.c5_do: Paste the playlist or channel URL. One transcript per video or episode. With Video kept, playlist files go under output/<playlist title>/ at ≤720p.
cases.c6_do: Use Files & folders. Power (or Custom) can scan subfolders recursively.
cases.c7_want: Another program on this PC should submit jobs
cases.c7_do: Tools & advanced → REST API (127.0.0.1 only). Open Swagger at http://127.0.0.1:8788/v1/docs when the API badge shows on.
cases.c8_want: Slides, screenshots, or PDFs to text
cases.c8_do: Tools & advanced → Vision / OCR → Gemini Vision plus a Google API key. Dropped images otherwise error.

speakers.title: Who spoke (Person 1 / Person 2)
speakers.intro: Ordinary transcription writes what was said and when. It does not mark speakers. Person tags are opt-in and never invent real names (Teams-style names are not available).
speakers.path_a_1: General → Also save… → Export timed transcript as WebVTT.
speakers.path_a_2: Default video language = English (not Auto). Also set English on the queue row for that item.
speakers.path_a_3: Tools & advanced → Speaker labels → Label speakers (Person 1 / Person 2).
speakers.path_a_4: Save Preferences. The app uses model ggml-small.en-tdrz (download Whisper models if prompted).
speakers.path_a_5: Run the job again. New .vtt cues start with <v Person 1> or <v Person 2>.
speakers.path_b_title: Path B — any language (pyannote after Whisper)
speakers.path_b_1: WebVTT on. Whisper language can stay Russian, Ukrainian, Auto, etc.
speakers.path_b_2: Tools & advanced → Speakers (pyannote): HF token, Python path, then Diarize speakers after transcription.
speakers.path_b_3: Needs a local Python venv with pyannote (see tools/diarize next to the project / release notes).
speakers.why_1: Label speakers was never saved (checkbox stays grey until language is English).
speakers.why_2: Language was Auto / Russian / Ukrainian — tinydiarize is skipped on purpose so it does not force English and ruin the transcript.
speakers.why_3: The queue row kept an older language; changing Default video language does not rewrite rows already in the queue.
speakers.why_4: You opened an old .vtt from a run before speakers were enabled.

modes.title: Transcription modes
modes.cloud_body: OpenAI-compatible POST …/audio/transcriptions. Key lives in the OS credential store. Typical: api.openai.com/v1 + whisper-1. Large files are split automatically.
modes.local_body: Fully local. For meeting quality use large-v3 with a GPU whisper-cli build when available. medium is a solid CPU default; large-v3-turbo is faster but can hallucinate — verify on your audio.
modes.browser_body: No whisper-cli. Fine for short clips. Do not use large-v3 here — the webview often crashes. Cap is medium. For quality, switch to On this computer.
modes.subs_body: Optional fast path: if a single video has manual subtitles in a priority language, the app can fetch SRT and skip Whisper. Auto-generated captions are ignored. Playlists always go through download + Whisper.

outputs.title: What gets saved
outputs.intro: Plain .txt is always written. Optional siblings are toggled under General → Also save… or with the chips on the queue.
outputs.txt: .txt — full transcript text (same wording as timed cues when WebVTT is on).
outputs.vtt: .vtt — timed WebVTT cues; required for speaker labels.
outputs.srt: .srt — original YouTube subtitle file when the captions fast path runs and Keep SRT is on.
outputs.video: Video — keep the downloaded file (playlists: folder per playlist, ≤720p).
outputs.audio: Audio — keep extracted audio (m4a / mp3 / original).
outputs.info: .info.json — title, URL, channel, dates from yt-dlp.

cookies.title: YouTube / TikTok downloads
cookies.intro: Some videos need a logged-in browser session (age gate, login wall). Set cookies under Tools & advanced.
cookies.win_body: Use Firefox: log into YouTube there, then set Cookies source = Firefox and Save. Chrome / Edge often fail because of app-bound cookie encryption — closing the browser does not fix that.
cookies.auto_body: If cookie copy/decrypt fails, the download retries once without cookies. Public videos often succeed; age-gated ones still need working Firefox cookies.
cookies.deno_body: Some YouTube extraction paths need Deno (or Node). If you see “no supported JavaScript runtime”, install Deno and set yt-dlp JS runtimes to deno in the same Tools section.
cookies.tiktok_body: Downloads are paced (default ~20 s between starts + jitter) to reduce IP blocks. Photo posts and bare profile URLs are unsupported on purpose.

map.title: Where to click
map.intro: Preferences sections and what lives there. Profile Simple hides Vision, speakers, REST, and recursive folder scan.
map.m2w: General → Also save…, or queue chips
map.m4: Cloud / local / in-app mode, Whisper model
map.m5: Manual captions, priority languages, keep SRT
map.m6: ffmpeg, yt-dlp, Deno, cookies, download pause
map.m11: Retry failed URL; save still-broken links
map.m12w: Always on — dual panels with separate Stop

limits.title: Limits
limits.l1: Speaker labels are Person 1 / Person 2 — not real names from Teams or Zoom.
limits.l2: Tinydiarize (Label speakers) is English-only. Use pyannote for other languages.
limits.l3: In-app WASM is not for large-v3 or long heavy jobs.
limits.l4: Cloud providers may limit request size; the app splits and merges when possible.
limits.l5: Chromium cookies on Windows are unreliable for yt-dlp; prefer Firefox.
limits.l6: Stop batch cancels running and pending jobs and kills child processes.
limits.l7: Changing Default video language does not change items already in the queue.
limits.l8: Unsaved Preferences are not used until you click Save changes.
